process_observations.observation: N3-F-03 is the second of the two failure shapes admin/record-types-and-page-layouts/references/metadata-examples.md's layout-required-fields table names ('Field:<F> must be Required', for a field already present with the wrong behavior), distinct from run 1's N3-F-02 ('Layout must contain an item for required layout field: <F>', for a field with no entry at all). The repair procedure this build already had in deploy-order.md §3 item 2 named both shapes and their fixes before either was hit, so this run applied a documented fix rather than improvising one.

The re-run checker output is byte-for-byte the same finding set as the run-1 repair's re-run (one REVIEW merge-candidate finding, one INFO no-Profile-in-scope finding, exit 0), confirming the change to Name's behavior did not disturb anything else this checker inspects - in particular it did not create a new zero-Required-items INFO (both layouts already carry a Required item from run 1) and did not change the two files' equality (they are still identical after normalisation, since the same edit was applied to both).

Q11's answer - that must-fill enforcement for ordinary fields lives in validation rules, not on the layout - now has two platform-required exceptions on this one layout (Probability, Name) rather than one. Neither exception was requested by Q11 or Q20; both were discovered from the org after the fact. A third dry run finding a further exception would not be a surprise given gotchas.md #12's one-field-per-run pattern, and deploy-order.md §6 says so, but a reader skimming only Q11's answer and not §6 could still conclude no field on this layout is platform-required.

A25 now covers two fields but is still not closed - the same open status as after the run-1 repair, just with more evidence behind it. deploy-order.md §6's 'Second discovery' subsection restates the standing instruction to keep iterating scripts/mock_deploy.py. Two consecutive rounds each finding exactly one new item is not evidence the set is now complete; it is two data points on an unknown-length list.

This is the second time this step has been carried through built -> tested and then reset back through failed -> pending -> running for a repair discovered by the org. The plan's runs[] array for M1-S02 now holds seven entries across two build/test/doc-keeper cycles. Nothing here is wrong - the state machine is built for exactly this recovery path (standards/build-orchestration.md §4) - but a reader of plan.json who stops at the first tested entry rather than the last run would misread the step's current state.
